nativeSource.title: High performance communication by people with paralysis using an intracortical brain-computer interface
nativeSource.note: Primary study mean: 4.16 ± 0.39 bps on a 9×9 grid. A 6×6 condition reports 3.7 ± 0.4 bps; the slide’s chosen condition/statistic is unconfirmed. The photographed value remains approximate rather than silently replaced by either result.

nativeSource.title: PRIME Study Progress Update — User Experience (company report)
nativeSource.quote: He has subsequently achieved 8.0 BPS and is currently trying to beat scores of the Neuralink engineers using a mouse (~10 BPS).
nativeSource.note: The May 8, 2024 company update reports an 8.0-bps achievement; it does not identify the slide’s exact value/date/30×30 combination. The later October 1, 2026 post cites a previous 10.39-bps record without dating its achievement. Company claims are distinct from independently validated study results.

nativeSource.title: Motor neuroprosthesis implanted with neurointerventional surgery improves capacity for activities of daily living tasks in severe paralysis
nativeSource.quote: The participant achieved 1.33 (1.58, 0.94–1.58) bits/trial at an ITR of 0.46 (0.41, 0.28–0.63) bits s -1 with the motor neuroprosthesis alone, and 4.43 (4.95, 3.85–4.95) bits/trial at an ITR of 1.57 (1.40, 0.98–2.11) bits s -1 was transmitted with the motor neuroprosthesis + eye-tracker.
nativeSource.note: Participant 2 mean isolated motor-neuroprosthesis contribution: 0.46 bps; participant 1: 0.32. Actual typing used eye-tracking; the isolated contribution is an author estimate. Hybrid motor-neuroprosthesis plus eye-tracker results were 1.08 and 1.57 bps. The slide uses a 2021 placement; the exact selected statistic is unconfirmed.

nativeSource.title: High-performance brain-to-text communication via handwriting

rate.statistic: mean across four blocks on final evaluation day

nativeSource.quote: Notably, typing speeds were high, plateauing at 90 characters per minute with a mean character error rate of 5.4% (averaged across all four blocks on the final day) (Fig. 2c).
nativeSource.note: 90 cpm final day pairs with 5.4% CER / 94.6% character accuracy, not the overall 94.1% accuracy. Do not mix 6.18 bps author approximation into a common 6-bits/word series without a visibly separate metric category. Separate author technical report gives an approximate 6.18 bps using an empirical corrected-typing conversion; this is separate from the photographed coordinate.

nativeSource.title: Neuroprosthesis for Decoding Speech in a Paralyzed Person with Anarthria

rate.task: real-time visually prompted sentence decoding, language model enabled

nativeSource.quote: We decoded sentences from the participant’s cortical activity in real time at a median rate of 15.2 words per minute, with a median word error rate of 25.6%.
nativeSource.note: The median WER across blocks and median WPM across trials are source-level aggregate pairings, not a common per-trial information channel estimate. 50-word restricted vocabulary; a separate conversational demonstration should not be substituted for the measured prompted task.

nativeSource.title: A high-performance speech neuroprosthesis

rate.rate_pairing_scope: Headline mean pace is reported adjacent to the vocabulary-specific aggregate WER; not claimed to be separately measured at exactly 62 WPM for each condition.

nativeSource.quote: T12 achieved a 9.1% word error rate for the 50-word vocabulary across all vocalizing days (11.2% for silent) and a 23.8% word error rate for the 125,000-word vocabulary across all vocalizing days (24.7% for silent).
nativeSource.note: Do not combine 9.1% WER with the 125,000-word vocabulary; 9.1% is the 50-word vocalized condition. Unconstrained large vocabulary does not mean the reported evaluation was unprompted free conversation.

nativeSource.title: A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control

rate.task: real-time text decoding of held-out silently attempted prompted sentences

nativeSource.quote: We observed a median real-time decoding rate of 78.3 WPM (99% CI \[75.5, 79.4\]; Fig. 2f).
nativeSource.note: A 2024 author correction affects electrode anatomical assignments, not real-time decoding performance. 1,024-word online result must not be combined with 39,378-word offline simulation. Use 78 for a faithful rounded slide label or 78.3 for primary-text precision; do not silently pretend the original slide encoded that precision.

nativeSource.title: An Accurate and Rapidly Calibrating Speech Neuroprosthesis

rate.statistic: mean, final five copy-task evaluation sessions
rate.task: prompted copy task at self-paced speaking rate

nativeSource.quote: The mean decoding performance for the copy task in the final five evaluation sessions was a word error rate of 2.5% (95% CI, 2.0 to 3.1) at the participant’s self-paced speaking rate of 31.6 words per minute (95% CI, 31.2 to 32.0) (Fig. S1B), with individual daily mean word error rates ranging from 1.0 to 3.3% (Table S3).
nativeSource.note: Slide 33 WPM is not the final-paper aggregate 31.6 WPM. Use 31.6 paired with 2.5% WER, not 33. Do not silently substitute a final-day 32.8 WPM value for the five-session aggregate; 32.8 was not established from the excerpts retrieved in this worker.

nativeSource.title: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain-computer interface for speech and cursor control
nativeSource.dateBasis: bioRxiv v1 posting, not DOI date string; peer-reviewed online publication 2026-06-15

accuracy_measure.metric: participant-rated sentences at least mostly correct

nativeSource.quote: He communicated 183,060 sentences – totaling 1,960,163 words – at an average rate of 56.1 words per minute.
nativeSource.note: 56.1 WPM personal use cannot be paired with 99.2% prompted-copy word accuracy as if the same task. 92.3% sentence self-rating is not 7.7% WER. 2025 preprint is legitimate date for historical slide, but identify it explicitly; final paper belongs to 2026. Same participant as Card 2024, not an independent cohort. Preprint v1 posted July 7, 2025; final Nature Medicine paper published June 15, 2026. Self-rated sentence correctness is a different endpoint from WER.
